If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment reversal.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to align with historical mean reversion.  
If forecast deviates >3% from true value in early horizon and sentiment is positive, apply a downward correction of 1.0–1.5% to prevent overcorrection.  
If forecast deviates >3% from true value in late horizon and sentiment is negative, apply an upward correction of 1.0–1.5% to avoid underestimation.
